page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with marginal notes in the left margin. Running head at top with page number at top left. Main text in paragraphs, a verse heading and verse paragraph, then a final paragraph ending in a catchword at the right.

main_text.p: Credimus Deus iuste pariter & miseri-cors, te nequaquam esse ἐπηρόφθαλμον[?], ac te nō delectari impietate & iniustitia: nec comoraturos apud te malos: ideo miseret quidē nos aduersariorum nostrorum, qui malis nostris lætantur, vim nobis inferunt, diripiunt facultates nostras, & nos extorres & exules esse volunt, deserunt nos in istis angustiae nostrae diebus: illud verò nobis solatio est, quod terrena solū nobis eripiuntur, non cœlestia bona: quòd perfequutionem patimur iusticiæ causa, quòd quiduis mali falsò de nobis dicitur, Christi Iesu filij tui (in cuius solius iurauimus verba causa: q;[?] deserimur, sed ab ijs, qui tecum colligere, qui veram filiorum tuorum communionē, tueri, recusant. Cōuerte, quesō, ex his quos tibi integrum est, cæteros compesce. Da nobis ut palmæ in morem floreamus, ad laudem gratiæ tuæ, & ut respirare Ecclesia possit. Amen, Amen.
main_text.head: VERSUS XVI.

p.i: Lectio 10. post reditū die 27. Ap. 1584.Nam quum biberitis in monte sanctitatis meæ, bibent omnes gentes iugiter: bibet, inquam, & absorbebunt: erunt q;[?] ac si non fuissent.

page.notes: Greek word after "esse" read as ἐπηρόφθαλμον with doubt on the final letters; marked [?]. The abbreviation "q;" after "causa:" and after "erunt" is unclear and marked [?]. The reading "possit" is taken from the long-s form "pofsit". The running head line "ORATIO." is small centred type beneath the main running head; included with it. The catchword "loco" is at the right below the last line. Word "angustiae" is broken at the line end without a printed hyphen and is written whole. The marginal note at left is three lines of printed type, combined into one note.
